title: ThreadAtlas Step 0: Documents, Units, Pieces
subtitle: 19,395 documents split into 42,822 units, with a per-piece speaker table
description:
Every document in the IT 494 memory-backend corpus, split into units, with a piece table that says what each stretch of a file is and who is speaking there. 19,395 documents, 42,822 units, 224,522 pieces, produced in one pass by a public notebook for $6.64.

This is the input to a memory backend, not a finished analysis. Step 0 answers one question about a raw file: where does this document divide, and what kind of text is each part? No entities, no facts, no summaries.

**Not a chunker.** Nothing is cut on length. A language model reads a numbered list of the file's own lines and says where the front matter ends, where the body begins, where the notes and references and appendix are, and where each chapter or scene or turn starts. Units group those natural parts up to a size cap, cutting only at boundaries the model named and copied back so the copy could be checked against the line.

Two properties, verified on all 19,395 documents rather than asserted:

- Pieces and units tile the document. Every byte belongs to exactly one piece and exactly one unit, no gaps, no overlaps.
- A unit never mixes region kinds. It is all body, or all references, or all appendix, never running from the end of a chapter into the footnotes. A chat unit holds both user and assistant pieces, because those are the two sides of one conversation.

The piece table carries the speaker, so a quote's voice is the author of the piece holding it.

**Every document carries its text.** Nothing is withheld and no row needs rebuilding from a source file.

**Files.** `documents.jsonl` (19,395 rows: identity, title, author, date, full text), `units.jsonl` (42,822 rows: character ranges into that text), `pieces.jsonl` (224,522 rows: what each stretch is and who speaks), `attribution.jsonl` (100 rows: the CC-BY papers' authors, title, license, DOI and source URL), `receipt.json` (the run's own counts). `README.md`, `SCHEMA.md`, `METHOD.md`, `PROVENANCE.md` and `LIMITS.md` are in the dataset.

**Corpus.** 19,206 LongMemEval-S sessions, 31 volumes of Greek and Roman literature including five OCR'd institutional scans, 29 Oz books, 100 CC-BY papers on knowledge graphs and retrieval-augmented generation, 20 GraphRAG-Bench novels, and 9 Sherlock Holmes volumes. Three shapes on purpose: clean e-texts, damaged scans with heavy apparatus, and assistant chat logs.

**The papers are CC-BY, and attribution is a condition of that license.** `attribution.jsonl` gives each paper's authors, title, year, venue, DOI, OpenAlex id, exact license and source URL, joined to the documents on doc_id. Render the authors, the title and the license wherever a paper's text is shown or quoted.

**Licensing is layered.** Packaging, schema and every derived field are MIT. The literature is public domain in the United States by expiry of term. GraphRAG-Bench and LongMemEval are MIT and keep their own notices. The papers are CC-BY. See PROVENANCE.md.

**Known limits are documented, not hidden.** 59 documents carry a substantive flag; 46 pointers out of 224 mismatches could not be recovered and those breaks were dropped; 6 read units and 8 chat units are over the cap; 46 read documents carry no date because the run never infers one. LIMITS.md gives the counts and the diagnosis.

Made by https://www.kaggle.com/code/jhffmn/threadatlas-extractor (threadatlas-extractor 1.6, gpt-5.6-luna). Raw inputs: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/jhffmn/it494-narrative-corpora-raw

IT 494 directed project, Illinois State University, fall 2026.
userSpecifiedSources:
SOURCES. Project Gutenberg (29 Oz volumes, 9 Sherlock Holmes volumes, 26 volumes of Greek and Roman literature); Archive.org institutional scans (5 OCR'd Loeb and 19th-century volumes); GraphRAG-Bench novel contexts, MIT, https://github.com/GraphRAG-Bench/GraphRAG-Benchmark ; LongMemEval-S sessions, MIT, https://github.com/xiaowu0162/LongMemEval ; and 100 full-text papers on knowledge graphs and retrieval-augmented generation gathered from OpenAlex, every one of them Creative Commons Attribution.

COLLECTION. Every file was fetched by an idempotent, title-verifying script that records the source URL, byte count and sha256 per file. The raw inputs are published byte-identical, with those manifests, at https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/jhffmn/it494-narrative-corpora-raw . The two benchmark corpora were unpacked from their upstream JSON into one file per document; nothing was cleaned, normalised or truncated. The papers' license was read per paper from OpenAlex and recorded, never assumed; only Creative Commons works were kept.

PROCESSING. One pass of the public notebook https://www.kaggle.com/code/jhffmn/threadatlas-extractor (threadatlas-extractor 1.6, gpt-5.6-luna) over 19,395 files on 2026-09-09. The extractor sees a raw file and nothing else: no filename convention and no per-corpus rule. Each document is shown to the model as its own numbered lines; the model points at a line by number and copies that line's text, and a boundary is kept only when the copy verifies against the line it names. Units group the resulting pieces up to a 4,000-word cap, cutting only at boundaries the model named. Verified on all 19,395 exported documents: pieces and units tile every document with no gaps or overlaps, unit ids are unique and recompute from the text, positions are dense, and no unit mixes a region kind. Total cost $6.64, median $0.0135 per read document, nothing for the 19,206 chats. METHOD.md gives the full procedure.

LICENSING. Packaging, schema and every derived field are MIT. The literature is public domain in the United States by expiry of term. GraphRAG-Bench and LongMemEval are MIT and keep their own notices. The 100 papers are CC-BY: their text is redistributed here, and attribution.jsonl carries the authors, title, license, DOI and source URL that the license requires be rendered wherever the text is shown. No file is offered under a license its source did not grant. PROVENANCE.md gives this per corpus.

KNOWN LIMITS. 59 documents carry a substantive flag; 46 of 224 pointer mismatches could not be recovered and those breaks were dropped; 6 read units and 8 chat units exceed the word cap; 46 read documents carry no date because the run never infers one. LIMITS.md gives the counts and the diagnosis. This is not ground truth: there is no gold segmentation for these works, and what is verified is internal consistency plus the pointer gate.

PART OF the IT 494 directed project, Illinois State University, fall 2026.
